name: Type 2 diabetes
overview: A chronic condition affecting how the body processes blood sugar, caused by insulin resistance or reduced insulin production.
symptoms: Increased thirst and frequent urination
Fatigue and blurred vision
Unexplained weight loss
treatment: Typically managed with lifestyle changes, oral medication such as metformin, and in some cases insulin therapy. Regular blood glucose monitoring is essential.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Diabetes fact sheet

name: Hypertension
overview: Persistently elevated blood pressure in the arteries, often with no early symptoms, that raises the risk of heart disease and stroke.
symptoms: Usually asymptomatic in early stages
Headaches or shortness of breath at very high readings
Nosebleeds in severe cases
treatment: Managed through reduced sodium intake, regular exercise, weight management, and antihypertensive medication such as ACE inhibitors when prescribed.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Hypertension fact sheet

name: Dengue fever
overview: A mosquito-borne viral infection common in tropical and subtropical regions, transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
symptoms: High fever with severe headache
Pain behind the eyes, joint, and muscle pain
Skin rash and easy bruising
treatment: No specific antiviral treatment exists; care focuses on rest, fluids, and fever management. Warning signs such as bleeding or abdominal pain need urgent hospital care.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Dengue and severe dengue fact sheet

name: Typhoid fever
overview: A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, spread through contaminated food or water, common where safe sanitation is limited.
symptoms: Sustained high fever that rises gradually
Abdominal pain with constipation or diarrhea
Fatigue, headache, and loss of appetite
treatment: Treated with a prescribed course of antibiotics along with rest and hydration. Untreated cases can lead to serious complications, so medical diagnosis is important.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Typhoid fact sheet

name: Asthma
overview: A chronic condition in which the airways narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus, making breathing difficult and triggering wheezing episodes.
symptoms: Wheezing and shortness of breath
Chest tightness
Coughing, especially at night or early morning
treatment: Managed with inhaled bronchodilators for quick relief and inhaled corticosteroids for long-term control, alongside avoiding known triggers.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Asthma fact sheet

name: Common cold
overview: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat, usually caused by rhinoviruses, and one of the most frequent illnesses in adults and children.
symptoms: Runny or stuffy nose and sneezing
Sore throat and mild cough
Low-grade fever, mostly in children
treatment: Usually resolves on its own within a week; rest, fluids, and over-the-counter symptom relief can help. Antibiotics are not effective since it is viral.
sourceCitation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Common cold overview

name: Seasonal influenza
overview: A contagious viral respiratory illness that circulates seasonally, generally more severe than the common cold.
symptoms: Sudden high fever and chills
Body aches and fatigue
Dry cough and sore throat
treatment: Rest and fluids for most cases; antiviral medication may be prescribed early on for high-risk patients. Annual vaccination reduces risk.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Influenza fact sheet

name: Migraine
overview: A neurological condition causing recurrent, often one-sided headaches, frequently accompanied by sensitivity to light and sound.
symptoms: Throbbing headache, often on one side
Nausea and sensitivity to light or sound
Visual disturbances before onset in some cases
treatment: Managed with pain-relief medication for attacks and, for frequent migraines, preventive medication prescribed by a doctor along with trigger avoidance.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Headache disorders fact sheet

name: Acute gastroenteritis
overview: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually caused by viral, bacterial, or parasitic infection, leading to diarrhea and vomiting.
symptoms: Watery diarrhea and vomiting
Abdominal cramps
Dehydration signs such as thirst and reduced urination
treatment: Oral rehydration solution is the priority to prevent dehydration. Most cases resolve with supportive care, though severe or prolonged cases need medical attention.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Diarrhoeal disease fact sheet

name: Iron-deficiency anemia
overview: A condition where the body lacks enough healthy red blood cells due to insufficient iron, reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.
symptoms: Fatigue and weakness
Pale skin and shortness of breath
Dizziness and brittle nails
treatment: Addressed with dietary iron intake and iron supplementation as prescribed, alongside treating any underlying cause of blood loss.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Anaemia fact sheet

name: Peptic ulcer disease
overview: Sores that develop on the lining of the stomach or upper small intestine, often linked to H. pylori infection or long-term use of certain pain medications.
symptoms: Burning stomach pain, often between meals
Bloating and nausea
Dark or tarry stools in severe cases
treatment: Treated with acid-reducing medication and, when H. pylori is present, a course of antibiotics. Avoiding NSAIDs and irritants supports healing.
sourceCitation: Mayo Clinic, Peptic ulcer overview

name: Tuberculosis
overview: A bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, most commonly affecting the lungs, and spread through the air when an infected person coughs.
symptoms: Persistent cough lasting more than two weeks
Night sweats and unexplained weight loss
Fatigue and low-grade fever
treatment: Treated with a supervised, multi-drug antibiotic regimen over several months. Completing the full course is essential to prevent drug resistance.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Tuberculosis fact sheet

name: Chronic kidney disease
overview: A gradual loss of kidney function over time, often linked to diabetes and hypertension, which can progress silently in early stages.
symptoms: Swelling in the legs, ankles, or feet
Fatigue and reduced appetite
Changes in urination frequency or appearance
treatment: Managed by controlling underlying conditions such as blood pressure and blood sugar, dietary adjustments, and in advanced stages, dialysis or transplant.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Chronic kidney disease overview

name: Osteoarthritis
overview: The most common form of arthritis, caused by the gradual breakdown of joint cartilage, leading to pain and stiffness most often in weight-bearing joints.
symptoms: Joint pain that worsens with activity
Stiffness, especially after rest or in the morning
Reduced range of motion and joint swelling
treatment: Managed with pain relief medication, physical therapy, weight management, and in severe cases, joint replacement surgery.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Osteoarthritis fact sheet

name: Malaria
overview: A mosquito-borne disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, transmitted through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes, common in parts of South Asia including India and Nepal.
symptoms: Fever with chills and sweating
Headache and body aches
Fatigue and nausea
treatment: Treated with a prescribed course of antimalarial medication specific to the parasite species. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to prevent severe complications.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Malaria fact sheet

name: Rabies
overview: An almost always fatal viral infection of the nervous system, transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal, most often dogs. South Asia, particularly India, carries a significant share of the global rabies burden.
symptoms: Fever and tingling at the bite site
Anxiety, confusion, or agitation as the disease progresses
Difficulty swallowing and muscle spasms in later stages
treatment: Immediate wound washing with soap and water followed by urgent post-exposure prophylaxis (vaccine, and immunoglobulin if indicated) at a medical facility is critical. Rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear, making emergency care after any bite or scratch essential rather than optional.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Rabies fact sheet

name: Snakebite envenoming
overview: Tissue and organ damage caused by venom injected through the bite of a venomous snake. South Asia, especially India, has one of the highest snakebite death tolls in the world.
symptoms: Pain and swelling around the bite
Bleeding, bruising, or blistering
Difficulty breathing or drooping eyelids in severe envenoming
treatment: Requires urgent transport to a medical facility for antivenom and supportive care. Keep the affected limb still and below heart level, and avoid cutting, sucking, or applying a tight tourniquet to the wound.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Snakebite envenoming fact sheet

name: Leprosy
overview: A chronic infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae that mainly affects the skin, nerves, and eyes. India accounts for a large share of new cases diagnosed worldwide each year.
symptoms: Pale or reddish skin patches with reduced sensation
Numbness or weakness in the hands, feet, or face
Thickened or enlarged peripheral nerves
treatment: Fully curable with multidrug therapy taken over several months to a year. Early treatment prevents the nerve damage and disability historically associated with the disease.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Leprosy fact sheet

name: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis)
overview: A parasitic disease spread by sandfly bites that affects internal organs, concentrated in the Bangladesh-India-Nepal 'kala-azar belt' of South Asia.
symptoms: Prolonged fever lasting more than two weeks
Weight loss and an enlarged spleen or liver
Fatigue and low blood cell counts
treatment: Treated with antileishmanial medication under medical supervision. The region has made significant progress toward elimination through combined vector control and treatment programs.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Leishmaniasis fact sheet

name: Japanese encephalitis
overview: A viral brain infection spread by Culex mosquitoes, most common in rural farming areas of South Asia and Southeast Asia, particularly where rice cultivation and pig farming create mosquito breeding conditions.
symptoms: High fever and headache
Confusion or difficulty waking
Seizures or muscle weakness in severe cases
treatment: No specific antiviral treatment exists; care focuses on hospital-based supportive treatment. Vaccination is the primary prevention strategy in endemic areas.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Japanese encephalitis fact sheet

name: Chikungunya
overview: A mosquito-borne viral illness transmitted by the same Aedes mosquitoes that spread dengue, causing outbreaks across South Asia including India and Bangladesh.
symptoms: Sudden fever with severe joint pain
Muscle pain and headache
Rash and joint swelling that can persist for weeks
treatment: No specific antiviral treatment exists; managed with rest, fluids, and pain relief. Joint pain can linger for weeks to months after the initial illness.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Chikungunya fact sheet

name: Hepatitis A
overview: A viral liver infection spread through contaminated food or water, common in regions with limited access to safe sanitation across South Asia.
symptoms: Fatigue and nausea
Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice)
Abdominal discomfort and dark urine
treatment: Usually resolves on its own with rest, fluids, and avoiding alcohol while the liver heals; there is no specific antiviral treatment. Vaccination provides effective prevention.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Hepatitis A fact sheet

name: Rheumatic heart disease
overview: Permanent heart valve damage caused by one or more episodes of rheumatic fever, an inflammatory reaction to untreated streptococcal throat infection. It remains a significant cause of heart disease in South Asia.
symptoms: Shortness of breath, especially with activity
Fatigue and swelling in the legs or abdomen
Irregular heartbeat or chest discomfort
treatment: Managed with medication to control heart failure symptoms and prevent further strep infections. Severe valve damage may eventually require surgical repair or replacement.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Rheumatic heart disease fact sheet

name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
overview: A progressive lung disease that narrows the airways, commonly linked to smoking and indoor air pollution from biomass cooking fuels — a major risk factor across South Asia.
symptoms: Persistent cough with mucus
Shortness of breath that worsens over time
Wheezing and chest tightness
treatment: Managed with inhaled bronchodilators and, in some cases, corticosteroids, alongside quitting smoking and reducing exposure to indoor smoke. Pulmonary rehabilitation can help with severe symptoms.
sourceCitation: World Health Organization, Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease fact sheet
